players.product: InP high-speed response photodiodes (100G and 200G per lane) and monitor photodiodes for optical transceivers

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 (year ended March 31, 2026): net sales JPY 113,832 million (+3.1%), business profit JPY 39,352 million (+3.4%), operating profit JPY 38,097 million (-4.1%) and profit attributable to owners of parent JPY 28,009 million (+1.0%). In the photonics business, shipments of products for data-center optical transceivers and for telecommunications equipment expanded; automotive anti-reflection film (ARF) sales rose slightly; phosphor film sales ended at the end of the prior year's first half, while high-value camera-module products for high-end smartphones such as shaped anisotropic conductive film (ACF) grew. The initial plan (May 12, 2025) was net sales JPY 103,500 million and business profit JPY 29,000 million; the revised plan (November 12, 2025) was JPY 114,000 million and JPY 39,000 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Net sales JPY 113,832 million (+3.1%); business profit JPY 39,352 million (+3.4%); EBITDA JPY 46,892 million; ROIC 22.8%; ROE 27.3%

quarterly_data.signal: Electronic Materials Components segment, FY2026: optical semiconductors - demand for data-center optical transceiver products and telecommunications-equipment products grew, the company worked on yield improvement and shipment volumes expanded; secondary protection fuses - volumes grew on the production recovery at the main power-tool customer and continued sales of products for data-center battery backup units (BBU); shaped ACF for high-end smartphone camera modules was strong. Business profit rose despite higher growth investment in optical semiconductors. Production (at selling prices) was JPY 67,595 million (113.0% of the prior year). Optical Materials Components segment: sales JPY 47,971 million (-5.3%), business profit JPY 14,308 million (-1.7%). The group mainly produces to forecast, so it reports no orders received.
quarterly_data.figure: Electronic Materials Components sales JPY 66,724 million (+10.4%), business profit JPY 25,043 million (+6.5%); Optical Materials Components sales JPY 47,971 million (-5.3%)

quarterly_data.signal: Customer Restar: JPY 36,940 million, 32.5% of FY2026 net sales (FY2025: JPY 14,560 million, 13.2%). In the segment notes, Restar and its subsidiaries account for JPY 56,429 million of FY2026 revenue (FY2025: JPY 31,741 million), in both the Optical Materials and Electronic Materials segments. Restar Dexerials Taiwan, Restar Dexerials Korea and Restar Dexerials Hong Kong (49.0% equity-method affiliates) sell the company's products mainly in Taiwan, Korea and China.
quarterly_data.figure: JPY 36,940 million; 32.5% of FY2026 net sales

quarterly_data.signal: Customer Nitto Denko: JPY 12,959 million, 11.4% of FY2026 net sales (FY2025: JPY 13,671 million, 12.4%); Optical Materials Components segment.
quarterly_data.figure: JPY 12,959 million; 11.4% of FY2026 net sales

quarterly_data.signal: Medium-term plan 2028 refresh (announced May 13, 2026), positioning photonics as the growth driver: the business plan for FY2027-FY2029 was revised, with targets for the final year (fiscal year ending March 2029) of net sales JPY 164.0 billion, business profit JPY 63.0 billion, EBITDA margin 45%, EPS JPY 263, ROIC about 19% and ROE about 31%.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2029 targets: net sales JPY 164.0 billion; business profit JPY 63.0 billion; EBITDA margin 45%; EPS JPY 263

quarterly_data.signal: Management states that demand centred on data-center optical semiconductors is increasingly likely to expand on a scale exceeding earlier assumptions, and that capturing it requires stronger production capacity and a resilient supply system including the supply chain. In photonics, demand for optical semiconductors and optical-transceiver-related products is growing faster than initially assumed as data centers advance and scale up, while faster communication speeds are accelerating technology change; the group will concentrate R&D investment on differentiated technologies such as silicon-photonics-compatible devices and high-speed response photodiodes and strengthen production to meet demand.

R&D, FY2026: focus areas are photonics and semiconductor integration, under a medium- to long-term technology strategy looking toward opto-electronic convergence. At OFC 2025 (San Francisco) and CIOE 2025 (Guangdong, China) the company gave live demonstrations of waveguide photodiodes under development and surface-illuminated photodiodes in mass production.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D expense JPY 6,740 million (Optical Materials JPY 3,561 million; Electronic Materials JPY 3,179 million)

quarterly_data.signal: Capex FY2026 JPY 16,774 million (including right-of-use assets): Electronic Materials Components JPY 8,656 million, mainly optical-semiconductor buildings and machinery; Optical Materials Components JPY 2,920 million, mainly anti-reflection film equipment; corporate JPY 5,198 million. Major projects in progress or planned (as of March 31, 2026): Kanuma Plant No. 2 (Kanuma, Tochigi) building JPY 29,750 million (JPY 19,150 million paid), July 2023 to June 2026; a further Kanuma Plant No. 2 building JPY 9,629 million (JPY 3,790 million paid), December 2024 to September 2027; Kanuma Plant No. 2 Electronic Materials manufacturing equipment JPY 3,514 million (JPY 1,062 million paid), December 2024 to March 2029; head office / Tochigi site (Shimotsuke) Optical Materials building JPY 5,100 million, May 2026 to July 2027, and manufacturing equipment JPY 6,540 million, May 2026 to January 2028. The added capacity is not stated.
